chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah and Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
That which is recorded/accepted from recitation and supplication is only that which one hears with oneself.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a recitation or supplication to be considered valid according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the technical requirements for the validity of Quranic recitation and supplication, emphasizing that the reciter must audibly perceive their own voice. This criterion ensures mindfulness (khushu') and distinguishes formal ritual recitation from silent internal reflection, a point of discussion among Shia jurists regarding the minimum volume required for the act to be considered complete.
